newsitem.title: USA: Vermont lawmaker proposes property tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Vermont lawmaker proposes property tax reform.

text.p: NEW YORK, Dec 17 (Reuter) The chairman of the state's Democratic Party, State Representative Steven Howard of Rutland, has proposed reforming Vermont's property tax system.

Howard said his plan would eliminate the 70 percent of local property taxes currently used to fund education. Instead, he suggested that the state pick up the tab, funding education with a four-percent surcharge on income tax, a two-percent increase in corporate taxes, a two cent-a-gallon gasoline tax, and the first-ever state-wide tax on non-residential property.
Property tax reform, a hot topic in the November elections, is expected to be a focus of the upcoming legislative session.

However, Howard's plan likely will face stiff opposition from Senate Republicans, who have blocked property tax reform in recent legislative sessions. And Gov Howard Dean, a Democrat, has also pledged to oppose an increased income taxes to reform property tax.
